subject: Government
title: Political Culture and Socialization
outline: Meaning and importance of political socialization

modules.title: Political Culture
modules.html:
Political culture is the pattern of beliefs, attitudes, values, sentiments and orientations that a people hold towards their political system and their own role within it. It is, in short, the political personality of a society. The concept was popularised by Gabriel Almond and Sidney Verba in The Civic Culture (1963).

TypeOrientation of citizensTypical setting
ParochialLittle or no awareness of the national political system; loyalty to clan or village.Remote traditional communities.
SubjectAware of government and its output, but passive – they obey rather than participate.Authoritarian or military regimes.
ParticipantAware, informed and actively involved in inputs (voting, party work, protest).Mature democracies.

Almond and Verba argued that stable democracy rests on a civic culture, a balanced mixture of all three in which participation is tempered by deference and trust. Political culture may also be described as dominant (shared by the majority) or a sub-culture (held by an ethnic, regional or religious minority). Where sub-cultures conflict sharply, the culture is called fragmented; Nigeria's ethnic and religious cleavages illustrate this.

examples.q: A villager who has never heard of the National Assembly exhibits which political culture?
examples.a: A parochial political culture – there is no awareness of, or orientation towards, the national political system.

modules.title: Political Socialization and Its Agents
modules.html:
Political socialization is the lifelong process by which individuals acquire their political values, attitudes and patterns of behaviour. It transmits political culture from one generation to the next.

Agents of political socialization:

  • The family — the earliest and most enduring agent; children absorb party loyalties and attitudes to authority.
  • The school — civic education, debating societies, prefect elections, the national anthem and pledge.
  • Peer groups — friends and age-grades shape opinions, especially in adolescence.
  • Religious institutions — churches and mosques preach values of obedience, justice and communal duty.
  • The mass media — newspapers, radio, television and now social media set the agenda of public debate.
  • Political parties and pressure groups — rallies, manifestos and campaigns.
  • Government agencies — NYSC, National Orientation Agency, INEC voter education.
  • The workplace and trade unions.

Importance: it produces loyal and informed citizens, promotes national integration, stabilises the political system, recruits future leaders, and legitimises the regime.

examples.q: Name two government agencies used for political socialization in Nigeria and state their contribution.
examples.a: The National Youth Service Corps posts graduates outside their state of origin to promote national unity; the National Orientation Agency runs campaigns on civic responsibility and values.

modules.title: Political Participation and Political Apathy
modules.html:
Political participation covers all voluntary activities by which citizens influence the selection of rulers and the making of policy. Ranked from least to most demanding: discussing politics, voting, attending rallies, joining a party, campaigning, contributing funds, contesting elections, holding office.

Political apathy is a lack of interest or indifference to political activity. Causes include:

  • Illiteracy and ignorance of political processes.
  • Electoral malpractice, rigging and violence, which convince voters that their vote does not count.
  • Poverty and preoccupation with survival.
  • Broken promises and corruption — loss of confidence in politicians.
  • Long distances to polling units and cumbersome registration.
  • Fear of victimisation; religious or cultural restrictions.

Remedies: mass civic education, free and fair elections, use of technology such as BVAS to protect the vote, decent polling arrangements, punishment of electoral offenders, and responsive government that visibly delivers services.

examples.q: Suggest two practical measures to reduce voter apathy in Nigeria.
examples.a: (i) Sustained voter education by INEC and the National Orientation Agency, especially in rural areas. (ii) Credible, transparent elections with results transmitted electronically so citizens see that their votes count.

modules.title: Political Culture in Nigeria
modules.html:
Nigeria's political culture is best described as fragmented and transitional. Its main features are:

  • Ethnicity and regionalism — voters often support candidates from their own group, producing a politics of identity rather than of issues.
  • Godfatherism and patron–client politics — sponsorship of candidates in exchange for patronage.
  • Religion as a strong political marker, especially along the northern–southern divide.
  • The prebendal use of office — public office treated as an opportunity for private gain.
  • Militarised attitudes inherited from long years of military rule: intolerance of opposition, command style.
  • Growing civic assertiveness among urban youth, expressed through social media and mass protests.

Nation-building instruments — the federal character principle, NYSC, unity schools, quota admissions and a national language policy — are deliberate attempts to build a common participant culture out of these fragments.

examples.q: Why is Nigeria's political culture called 'transitional'?
examples.a: Because it is moving from largely parochial and subject orientations, reinforced by decades of military rule, towards a participant culture, without having fully arrived; elements of all three co-exist.

modules.title: Types: parochial, subject and participant
modules.html:
Types: parochial, subject and participant is a key part of Political Culture and Socialization (SSS 1, Government). Master the meaning, the main points and how it is tested in JAMB and WAEC questions on this topic.

Key points

  • Type Orientation of citizens Typical setting Parochial Little or no awareness of the national political system; loyalty to clan or village.
  • Subject Aware of government and its output, but passive – they obey rather than participate.
  • Participant Aware, informed and actively involved in inputs (voting, party work, protest).
  • Nation-building instruments — the federal character principle, NYSC, unity schools, quota admissions and a national language policy — are deliberate attempts to build a common participant culture out of these fragments.
  • Subject culture is passive awareness.

Worked example

Q: Citizens who are aware of government but do not participate display a
A: Subject culture — Subject culture is passive awareness.

Q: A political culture in which people are totally unaware of the national system is
A: Parochial — Parochial orientation is limited to the local community.

quiz.q: Political culture was popularised by
quiz.solution: The Civic Culture (1963) by Gabriel Almond and Sidney Verba.

quiz.q: Citizens who are aware of government but do not participate display a
quiz.solution: Subject culture is passive awareness.

quiz.q: A political culture in which people are totally unaware of the national system is
quiz.solution: Parochial orientation is limited to the local community.

quiz.q: Political socialization means
quiz.solution: It is the learning process that transmits political culture.

quiz.q: The earliest agent of political socialization is the
quiz.solution: The family is first and most enduring.

quiz.q: Which is NOT an agent of political socialization?
quiz.solution: Territory is an element of the state, not an agent of socialization.

quiz.q: The NYSC contributes to political socialization mainly by
quiz.solution: Cross-posting corps members promotes unity.

quiz.q: Political apathy means
quiz.solution: Apathy is lack of interest in political activity.

quiz.q: A major cause of voter apathy in Nigeria is
quiz.solution: Rigging convinces voters their ballots do not count.

quiz.q: The highest form of political participation is
quiz.solution: Holding office is the most demanding form.

quiz.q: A blend of parochial, subject and participant orientations is called
quiz.solution: Almond and Verba's civic culture.

quiz.q: Godfatherism in Nigerian politics is an example of
quiz.solution: Sponsorship in exchange for patronage is clientelism.

quiz.q: Which agency conducts voter education in Nigeria?
quiz.solution: The Independent National Electoral Commission.

quiz.q: Sub-culture in politics refers to
options: Values held by a minority group
quiz.solution: A minority pattern differing from the dominant culture.

quiz.q: Political participation is best encouraged by
quiz.solution: Education plus credible elections restore confidence.

quiz.q: The federal character principle is designed to
options: Ensure fair representation of all groups
quiz.solution: It spreads appointments across states and groups to build unity.

quiz.q: Political socialization begins in the:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2021). Correct answer: Family.

quiz.q: The process of learning political values and culture is called...
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2024). Correct answer: Political socialization.

quiz.q: Political socialization typically begins in the:
quiz.solution: Past question (WAEC 2025). Correct answer: Family.

quiz.q: Which of these is a primary agent of political socialization?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: The Family.

quiz.q: What is ‘Political Culture’?
options: Patterns of orientation toward political action and belief
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: Patterns of orientation toward political action and belief.

quiz.q: The first political party in Nigeria was the _____.
quiz.solution: The Nigerian National Democratic Party (NNDP), founded by Herbert Macaulay in 1923, was the first formal political party in Nigeria.

quiz.q: The first political party in Nigeria was:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2022). Correct answer: NNDP.

quiz.q: The first political party in Nigeria (NNDP) was formed in?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: 1923.

quiz.q: The first political party in Nigeria (formed 1923) was the?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: NNDP.

quiz.q: The Yoruba pre-colonial political system was based on the principle of _____.
quiz.solution: The Old Oyo Empire utilized a system of checks and balances where the Oyomesi (King makers) could check the powers of the Alaafin (the King).

quiz.q: Pressure groups differ from political parties in that they _____.
quiz.solution: Unlike political parties that seek to control state power by winning elections, pressure groups only seek to influence government decisions in favor of their members.

quiz.q: The pre-colonial Igbo political system was described as acephalous because _____.
options: it was led by powerful kings
it was governed by the military
quiz.solution: 'Acephalous' means 'headless'. The Igbo system was decentralized, based on village assemblies and age grades rather than a single monarch.

quiz.q: Socialism is an economic and political system based on _____.
options: private ownership of means of production
state ownership of means of production
quiz.solution: Socialism advocates that the means of production, distribution, and exchange should be owned or regulated by the community as a whole.

quiz.q: The document that contains the rules of a political party is the _____.
quiz.solution: While the manifesto contains the party's plans/promises, the party's constitution contains the internal rules and structure.

quiz.q: The process by which an individual is integrated into the political system and acquires political values is _____.
quiz.solution: Political socialization is the lifelong process by which people form their political ideas and acquire political values.

quiz.q: The administrative structure of a political party is usually headed by the _____.
quiz.solution: The National Chairman is typically the head of the party's executive committee and its administrative leader.

quiz.q: A state with a single political party is described as:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2022). Correct answer: Totalitarian.

quiz.q: In the pre-colonial Yoruba political system, the Oyomesi were:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2022). Correct answer: Kingmakers.

quiz.q: The manifesto of a political party is its:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2022). Correct answer: Proposed programme.

quiz.q: The pre-colonial Yoruba political system was characterized by...
options: A system of checks and balances
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2024). Correct answer: A system of checks and balances.

quiz.q: The pre-colonial Igbo political system was described as...
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2024). Correct answer: Acephalous (Segmentary).

quiz.q: Pressure groups differ from political parties because they...
options: Seek to influence government policy rather than capture power
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2024). Correct answer: Seek to influence government policy rather than capture power.

quiz.q: The Igbo pre-colonial political system was:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2025). Correct answer: Acephalous (Decentralized).

quiz.q: Fascism was a political ideology associated with:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2025). Correct answer: Benito Mussolini.

quiz.q: Fascism as a political movement started in?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: Italy.

quiz.q: The head of the 1986 Political Bureau was?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: Samuel Cookey.

quiz.q: What is ‘Communism’ as an economic and political system?
options: State/Public ownership of the means of production
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: State/Public ownership of the means of production.

quiz.q: The highest court of appeal in Nigeria during the colonial era was the _____.
options: Judicial Committee of the Privy Council
quiz.solution: Before Nigeria became a republic in 1963, the final appellate body was the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council in London.

quiz.q: The first indigenous Governor-General of Nigeria was _____.
quiz.solution: Dr. Nnamdi Azikiwe became the first indigenous Governor-General in 1960 and later the first President when Nigeria became a Republic in 1963.

quiz.q: The 'Elective Principle' was first introduced in Nigeria by the _____.
quiz.solution: The 1922 Clifford Constitution introduced the elective principle, which allowed for the first time the election of four representatives to the Legislative Council (3 for Lagos, 1 for Calabar).

quiz.q: The first military coup d'état in Nigeria occurred on _____.
quiz.solution: The first coup was led by Major Chukwuma Kaduna Nzeogwu on January 15, 1966, bringing an end to the First Republic.

quiz.q: The administrative structure of Nigeria's foreign policy is headed by the _____.
quiz.solution: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs is the government body responsible for the day-to-day management of Nigeria's external relations.

quiz.q: The system of 'Indirect Rule' was introduced in Nigeria by _____.
quiz.solution: Lord Lugard implemented the policy of using traditional rulers to govern the people under British supervision.

quiz.q: The first military coup in Nigeria occurred on _____.
quiz.solution: The first military coup, led by Major Chukwuma Kaduna Nzeogwu, took place on January 15, 1966, ending the First Republic.
